newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA'S CRICKET NURSERY TO GAIN 1.5 MLN RAND.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA'S CRICKET NURSERY TO GAIN 1.5 MLN RAND.

text.p: South Africa's nursery for the top cricketers of the future is to benefit by 1.5 million rand over the next three years, the United Cricket Board of South Africa (UCBSA) said on Wednesday.

"This magnificent sponsorship will secure a bright future for South African cricket, and a feature of this year's intake is the inclusion of three top young players from outside this country," UCBSA president Krish Mackerdhuj told reporters.
"This is all part of the United Cricket Board of South Africa's plan to assist in making Africa a leading cricket continent."

Sponsorship of the UCBSA's Plascon Academy will be increased by 600,000 rand over the three-year period -- with young cricketers from Uganda, Kenya and Zimbabwe also benefiting from the intensive coaching.

Kenyan all-rounder Thomas Odoyo, who starred for his country in last year's World Cup, and Zimbabwe test bowler Henry Olonga will join the likes of Free State left-arm spinner Nicky Boje and Eastern Province fast bowler Mornantau Hayward in the 1997 Plascon Academy intake.
Academy director Clive Rice said that Boje, a South African one-day international, had been included to develop his skills both as a cricketer and as a captain.
"We believe Nicky is right on the fringe of test selection and we want to make him an even better player. But we also feel that he has captaincy potential and this must also be exploited," Rice said.

"But the bottom line is that we are trying to get players -- a year or so out of school -- to find out if they really do want to play the game. We want players who are dead keen to play for South Africa."

The academy has been operating during the winter months for the last three years with recent participants including South African test batsman Adam Bacher and successful Natal captain Dale Benkenstein.

Plascon Academy squad for 1997: Nicky Boje (Free State), Loots Bosman (Griqualand West), Anthony Botha (Natal), Mark Bruyns (Natal), Jonathan Cook (Natal), Douglas Gain (Transvaal), Andrew Hall (Transvaal), Mornantau Hayward (Eastern Province), James Henderson (Transvaal), Pierre Joubert (Northern Transvaal), Guy Kimbowa Lutaaya (Uganda), Ryan Maron (Western Province), Robbie McQueen (Natal), Eugene Moleon (Western Province), Grant Morgan (Eastern Province), Thomas Odoyo (Kenya), Henry Olonga (Zimbabwe), Junaid September (Eastern Province), Morne Strydom (North West).
